No Shizuku? Set up with a PC instead

Permanent Proxy uses Shizuku to gain the same privileges as an ADB shell, so it no longer needs "Debug over Bluetooth".

1. Install Shizuku on your watch (sideload the APK, or install it from the Play Store on your phone and use "Apps on your phone").

2. Start Shizuku:
• Android 11 and newer: turn on Developer options → Wireless debugging, then open the Shizuku app and start it from there.
• Any Android 6.0+: connect the watch to a computer with adb and run:
 adb shell sh /storage/emulated/0/Android/data/moe.shizuku.privileged.api/start.sh
• Rooted? Just start Shizuku and choose root.

3. Start Shizuku again after every reboot (non-rooted devices only), then open Permanent Proxy and tap "Grant Shizuku permission".

Waiting for the Shizuku permission dialog.

Tap "Allow" when it appears.
If nothing happens, make sure Shizuku is running.
Open the Shizuku website on my phone
You chose "deny and don\'t ask again". Allow Permanent Proxy manually in the Shizuku app, then try again.
Could not ask Shizuku for permission. Is Shizuku running?

If you cannot or do not want to use Shizuku, you can give Permanent Proxy the "write secure settings" permission once from a computer. After that the app controls the proxy on its own.

1. Connect your watch to a computer with adb (Developer options → ADB debugging).

2. Run:

adb shell pm grant nl.jolanrensen.permanentproxy android.permission.WRITE_SECURE_SETTINGS

That is all. Reopen Permanent Proxy and set your proxy.

To undo this later:

adb shell pm revoke nl.jolanrensen.permanentproxy android.permission.WRITE_SECURE_SETTINGS

Note: this permission survives reboots, but it is removed when you reinstall the app.
